HOW MUCH SPACE DOES A PADEL COURT ACTUALLY NEED?
Padel court dimensions, explained
How much space do you need for a padel court? More than the court itself.

THE SPACE YOU NEED
Dashed footprint grows around the court: 36' (11M), 69' (21M)
PLAN FOR 36' X 69' (11m x 21m footprint)
Room for: RING BEAM, ACCESS, MACHINERY, GAMEPLAY

Start with the space. We recommend a thirty-six by sixty-nine foot footprint. That leaves room for the ring beam the court anchors into, comfortable access, machinery during installation, and good gameplay.

Footprint fills in as a concrete pad, then a cross-section with a slight tilt and water running off.
CONCRETE SLAB: 36' X 69' (2,484 SQ FT)
6-INCH POST-TENSIONED · 4,000 PSI
PITCHED 0.5-1% TO DRAIN

That footprint is your concrete slab: thirty-six by sixty-nine feet, about twenty-five hundred square feet. We build it six inches thick, post-tensioned, at least four thousand PSI, and pitched slightly so water runs off. Skip this and you'll see cracking, ponding, and turf failures.

Confirm: slab = full 36' x 69' (Sergio's quote uses 2,484 SF). Slope: the page says 0.5-1%, you've said 0.5-0.7% is best. The FSC brochure shows a rebar slab, not post-tensioned. Video will match the page unless you change it.

THE COURT
32'10" (10M) across, 65'7" (20M) along the side
65'7" X 32'10"
20m x 10m · 2,153 sq ft (200 m²) of turf
On that slab sits the court: sixty-five feet seven by thirty-two feet ten. That's twenty by ten meters, about two thousand one hundred fifty square feet of playing surface.

NET + SERVICE LINES
Net pulses, service lines draw.
NET: 2'11" CENTER, 3'0" POSTS (0.88m center, 0.92m posts)
SERVICE LINE: 22'10" FROM NET (6.95m from the net)

THE WALLS
Back wall: TOTAL HEIGHT 9'10" (3M), GLASS 6'7" (2M), MESH 3'3" (1M)
Side wall profile: 9'10" stepping to 6'7"
SIDES STEP DOWN TO 6'7" (2M)
Glass and mesh walls enclose the court. The back walls are nine feet ten: six feet seven of glass with three feet three of mesh above. The side walls step down to six feet seven toward the net.
Check: the side-wall step is drawn about 13 ft from the back wall (unlabeled). Confirm it matches your courts.

Court rotates to a compass: long axis north-south. Sun arc low in the east and west.
OUTDOORS: RUN IT NORTH-SOUTH
Outdoors, run the court's long axis north-south. East-west works, but the sun sits in players' eyes at sunrise and sunset.

INDOORS
Side view of the full court with ceiling lines.
MIN. CEILING 19'8" (6M)
COMPETITION: 23'-26'3" (7-8M)
19'8" OF CLEAR HEIGHT
Building indoors? You need at least nineteen feet eight of clear ceiling. Twenty-three feet for club play, twenty-six feet three for competition. Lights, ducts, and beams all go above that.
Match the page: show club 23' (7m) and competition 26'3" (8m) as separate lines.

Checklist ticks on one by one:
SETBACKS · HEIGHT LIMITS · FENCE + LIGHTING RULES · PERMITS
RULES VARY BY CITY
And check your city early. Setbacks, height limits, fence and lighting rules, and permits all vary.
